score_rationale: Strong willingness-to-pay validated by active commercial market: at least 5 major vendors (ContactOut, Ignite Data, CampaignLake, AverickMedia, Exact Data) currently selling real estate appraiser databases ranging from 47K to 100K+ records with quarterly updates and 85-90% accuracy guarantees. Four high-value B2B buyer segments: (1) appraisal management companies (AMCs) and lender panel managers recruiting appraisers for residential and commercial assignments — AMCs like Clear Capital, ServiceLink Valuation, Solidifi, and CoreLogic need constant appraiser pipeline expansion to meet lender demand for URAR (1004) and commercial appraisal reports, paying $3,000-$8,000/year for appraiser prospect lists; (2) real estate and mortgage technology vendors (RealtyTrac, a la mode WinTOTAL, Bradford Technologies ClickFORMS, CoreLogic Matrix) selling appraisal software, comparable sales databases, and USPAP compliance tools at $50-$200/month per appraiser — software vendors pay $5,000-$12,000/year for targeted appraiser marketing lists to acquire customers with $600-$2,400/year LTV; (3) continuing education providers selling mandatory state-required CE courses — all appraisers must complete 14-28 hours of continuing education biennially (7-hour USPAP update required every 2 years federally, plus additional state-specific hours) to maintain license renewal, creating recurring $150-$400 per appraiser every 2 years; (4) professional liability insurance carriers (OREP, LandAmerica, Hanover, The Hartford) selling E&O coverage required by AMCs and lenders for panel acceptance — premiums range $800-$2,500/year per appraiser depending on appraisal volume, property types (residential vs. complex commercial), and coverage limits. Federal ASC (Appraisal Subcommittee) maintains the national Appraiser Registry at asc.gov — a downloadable database of all State Licensed, State Certified Residential, and State Certified General Appraisers eligible to perform federally related transactions, updated monthly from all 50 state appraiser boards. Data includes appraiser full name, credential number, credential type (Licensed, Certified Residential, Certified General), issuing state, credential status (active, inactive, suspended), issue date, expiration date, and public disciplinary actions (current revocations, suspensions, voluntary surrenders). Zero PII — all credential and disciplinary data under Title XI federal law and state Freedom of Information laws. Engineering lift is low: single-source federal download from asc.gov Appraiser Registry (search/download functionality built-in), supplement with state-specific boards for additional fields (business name, address, phone where publicly listed), deduplicate multi-state credentials, normalize status codes. No affordable flat-file competitor exists on Gumroad or similar marketplaces — all existing vendors sell annual subscriptions ($3,000-$8,000/year) or pay-per-download models, leaving a clear gap for a one-time $99-$129 CSV. Audience size is substantial: approximately 100,000 active appraisers nationwide (88,442 as of ASC 2024 report), creating a TAM of 3,000+ potential B2B buyers across AMCs, appraisal software vendors, CE providers, and insurance carriers. Score is 8 due to validated high willingness-to-pay from multiple commercial vendors with quarterly update cycles and accuracy guarantees, confirmed federal ASC public registry with monthly updates and downloadable data, absence of low-cost flat-file alternatives, substantial appraiser population (100K), and four distinct B2B buyer segments with proven purchasing behavior in appraisal industry.

data_wanted: Federal ASC (Appraisal Subcommittee) maintains the national Appraiser Registry at asc.gov — a publicly accessible, searchable, and downloadable database of all State Licensed, State Certified Residential, and State Certified General Appraisers who are eligible to perform appraisals in connection with federally related transactions, updated monthly with data received directly from all 50 state appraiser regulatory agencies. ASC Appraiser Registry provides downloadable search results with complete listings of all appraisers or filtered by state/credential type. Key fields per credential: appraiser full name (first, middle initial, last), credential number (format varies by state, typically alphanumeric 5-10 characters), credential type (State Licensed, State Certified Residential, State Certified General), issuing state, credential status (active, inactive, suspended — registry only includes appraisers eligible for federally related transactions, so revoked credentials are excluded), issue date (initial credential issuance), expiration date (current credential expiration), and public disciplinary actions (the Appraiser Registry reports as public information active disciplinary actions that limit an appraiser's ability to appraise: current revocations, suspensions, and voluntary surrenders in lieu of discipline). Supplement federal ASC data with state-specific appraiser board databases for additional fields: business name/company affiliation, business address (street, city, state, ZIP — availability varies by state based on public records policies), phone number (where publicly listed), credential history (prior credentials, reinstatements), and detailed disciplinary records. All 50 state appraiser regulatory agencies maintain public license verification portals (examples: California OREA, Texas TALCB, Florida DBPR, New York DOS all provide searchable databases). Target all active credentials only (exclude inactive and suspended for primary product, optionally offer 'full registry with inactive' as premium tier). Scope to individual appraisers only — exclude AMC companies or appraisal firm entities. Approximately 100,000 active appraiser credentials nationwide as of 2026 (88,442 reported by ASC in 2024 Annual Report to Congress, modest growth expected). Target output: 100K rows, one per credential. Data is 100% public per Title XI federal law (Financial Institutions Reform, Recovery, and Enforcement Act of 1989) and state Freedom of Information laws — appraiser credentialing and disciplinary records are federally mandated public information.

(1) Appraisal management companies (AMCs): recruiting appraisers for lender panels is core business function — AMCs need constant pipeline expansion to meet assignment volume from mortgage lender clients; AMC business model depends on fast appraiser sourcing (72-hour typical turnaround SLA from lender to delivered appraisal report requires large appraiser pools); AMCs routinely pay $3,000-$8,000/year for appraiser prospect lists (confirmed by ContactOut, Ignite Data with quarterly update pricing models), making a $129 one-time CSV deliver 23×-62× cost savings. AMCs monetize each recruited appraiser at $200-$500/month in assignment fees. (2) Appraisal software vendors: a la mode, Bradford, CoreLogic generate $600-$2,400/year per appraiser in subscription revenue; vendors pay $5,000-$12,000/year for targeted appraiser marketing lists, making a $129 CSV deliver 39×-93× cost savings. A single acquired software customer yields 5×-19× ROI in year one. (3) Continuing education providers: all appraisers must complete 14-28 hours of CE biennially to maintain credentials (7-hour federal USPAP update + 7-21 additional state hours), creating mandatory recurring spend of $150-$400 per appraiser every 2 years; CE vendors pay $2,000-$5,000/year for appraiser databases, so a $129 CSV provides 15×-39× cost savings. (4) E&O insurance carriers: professional liability coverage is required by AMCs and lenders for panel acceptance, with premiums of $800-$2,500/year per appraiser; a single sold policy yields 6×-19× ROI vs. $129 database cost. The absence of any flat-file competitor below $500 (all existing vendors sell annual subscriptions $3,000-$8,000/year with quarterly updates or pay-per-download models, not one-time CSV downloads) combined with federal ASC downloadable registry (free but unsegmented/raw) creates a unique positioning: cleaned, deduplicated, enriched ASC data with state supplementation at one-time price with 23×-62× cost advantage over enterprise subscriptions.
